UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE REPORT OF THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE 2006-07-4 February 1, 2007 ESTABLISHMENT OF THE JOINT CLASSROOM STEERING COMMITTEE As approved by the Faculty Senate on February 22, 2007 BACKGROUND At the September 28 meeting of the Faculty Senate concerns about classrooms and responsibility for their equipment, design and maintenance were raised during the discussion of the spring 2006 faculty survey.
Ms.
Ann Morrissey, Director of Planning Services and Executive Assistant to the President, followed up immediately.
She noted that there were a number of ad hoc and informal groups responsible for various aspects of classroom support and management but no formal committee on classrooms.
Ms.
Morrissey brought the appropriate ad hoc groups and interested parties together, including the Faculty Senate Chair and Coordinator, to work on classroom issues.
In consultation with the President and the Provost, the Executive Committee proposes the establishment Joint classroom Steering Committee that will have Senate representation and will report regularly to the Faculty Senate.

RECOMMENDATION That the Faculty Senate approve the following charge to and membership of the Joint Classroom Steering Committee to be included in the UNIVERSITY MANUAL: 5.85.10 The Joint Classroom Steering Committee (JCSC) shall serve as a steering group to the functional areas that manage and have responsibility for classroom upkeep and planning (MTS, Enrollment Services, and Business Services).
The committee shall be responsible for the development of plans for all aspects of classroom planning and management, including, but not limited to, the development and management of a single classroom data-base, the establishment and updating of design standards, scheduling and planning, assessment of needs for classroom refurbishments and setting priorities, maintenance and ongoing management of classrooms and the coordination of resources for classroom upkeep and improvement.
This committee shall also monitor progress and the execution of these plans.

This committee shall be comprised of representatives from enrollment services, instructional technology, space planning, business services, property, facilities, the university architect, the president, the provost, and at least three representative of the faculty, one of whom shall be an academic department chair, appointed by the Faculty Senate.
The chairperson shall be selected by the committee and confirmed by the Faculty Senate and the President.

5.85.11 The JCSC shall form appropriate subcommittees, chaired by the representatives of the offices and groups identified in 5.85.10. These subcommittees shall meet regularly and report to the JCSC at each of its meetings. 5.85.12 The JCSC shall meet at least twice each semester and shall report annually to the Faculty Senate on the status of classrooms at the University.

In its present form, the committee and nominated Senators potentially have a two week window to be successful. Motion: Move nominating committee selection for Vice President and Executive Committee to December. Appendix C - By-Laws of the Faculty Senate Section 5. Election of Officers. 5.2 At its regular meeting in January December of each year the Senate shall elect a nominating committee of three members chosen from the members whose terms expire that May. This committee shall present two nominations for the position of Vice President/President-elect in February. The remaining one or two year positions on the Executive Committee shall be elected at the organizational meeting of the newly constituted Senate. In selecting its nominees for terms on the Executive Committee, the nominating committee shall consider the senators newly elected as well as those who have served for one or two years, shall consider continuity of membership, and shall, moreover, seek to maintain a reasonable distribution and rotation of the positions to be filled among the various colleges and schools. #04-05–25 , #10-11–29 , #14-15–25 , #20-21-5, #20-21-41

Date: 18 March 2022 Subject: Summary of JCSC allocations this year The JCSC has funds allocated annual for all General Assignment Classrooms on the Kingston campus.
The committee has allocated $400,000 annually for upgrades to Audio-visual technology and $300,000 for basic infrastructure within classrooms (e.g., chairs, tables, lecterns, blinds), so excludes big ticket items such as HVAC systems (which we are aware have issues in buildings but are beyond the committee).
The committee has a list of when all the AV technology in GAC classrooms has last been updated, and we try to upgrade equipment ~5 years.
Specific upgrades this year: Beaupre Projectors: Replace the outdated projectors in both Beaupre Lecture Halls with laser projectors $29,450 Ranger Hall Mac Minis Note- These new GACs will come online Fall 22- Summary: There are 11 GACs going online in Ranger hall as part of finishing the top 2 floors of the building.

On the project, classroom computers were listed as OFE (owner furnished equipment). $9,867 Computer upgrades: Computer upgrades for all the auditoria on campus along with other outdated machines in GAC classrooms $28,412.55 Active Learning Lite Classroom Quinn rms 214, 211, 209, Chafee 235, 244, 235, 251: Upgrade flat panel displays; Purchase 14 projectors as backup stock to replace projectors that cease to function: $69,834 Replace projection screens in Avedisian 170 and Ballentine 115. $10,448 Swan Hall Projector Replacement (16 Rooms) Summary: As we continue to work towards changing over all campus projectors to lasers (instead of lamps) swapping the entire buildings remaining lamp-based projectors out would be a bulk cost savings move.

It’s especially helpful in these spaces as newer projectors will always be brighter and all of Swan classrooms have windows which face towards the projected displays. $64,050 Lectern Furniture Update Summary: This project would allow for changing out the older solid wood lecterns in Chafee (2nd floor), Quinn (2nd floor), and Swan to the newer style lecterns that were put in place for the 21C project and in Bliss and Fascitelli Engineering building.
The metal lecterns allow for better airflow and

heat regulation of systems as well as offer ADA height adjustment to the primary instructor work surface. $116,050 AirMedia Wireless Presentation Device Updates Summary: We have various versions of the Crestron wireless presentation device deployed in classrooms based upon their installation year. Due to a Crestron program change, this means, from mobile devices, not all rooms are capable of fully mirroring device screens. This also results in there being 2 different Apps that instructors must know which one is the correct one to use with the device. Phasing out these older units eliminates this confusion and broadens system capability for faculty. This affects roughly 50 rooms. $51,396.40 Holdover Bill from FY 21: $11,683.40 Total spending to date: $391,191.13 Infrastructure fund: $300,000 annual allocation; We acquired 600 Learn2 chairs for 16 classrooms in Swan Hall (excluding Auditorium) using this year’s funds – those chairs were acquired for this academic year and the cost was $285,000. We also bought 16 accessible tables with adjustable height surfaces for the 16 classrooms in Swan Hall with remaining funds to accommodate students with disabilities for $15,000. Ken Sisson stated this was a problem for all classrooms on campus and there really needs to be greater efforts to provide infrastructure for students with disabilities.
